name: Single Permit, Highly Qualified Worker
summary: Work and residence permit for skilled workers with a Belgian employer. The employer applies to the region, then you get a long stay visa D.

eligibility.education: Level 6 qualification: higher education degree, or 3 years of relevant experience in the last 7 years, or ICT manager/specialist

income.note: 2026 gross threshold for Wallonia; 42,576 EUR (80%) if under 30. Thresholds are indexed yearly and may differ by region.

steps: Employer applies to the regional employment authority
Apply for visa D at a Belgian embassy or consulate
processing: Embassy says visa D takes a minimum of one week after the permit approval. Some files take longer.

name: European Blue Card
summary: Permit for highly paid, degree-level workers with a Belgian job offer.

eligibility.education: Higher education degree (3 years of study)

income.note: 2026 gross threshold listed by Wallonia; 55,052 EUR for juniors with under 3 years of experience. Brussels and Flanders may differ.

other: Contract of at least one year or indefinite. This came from an older Brussels page, so recheck.

name: Self-Employed Professional Card and Visa D
summary: Self-employed people need a professional card from the region where the business will be, then a long stay visa D.

other: Official pages read did not give detailed conditions or fees. Check the regional authority.

steps: Apply for the professional card from the regional authority
Apply for visa D at the embassy

name: Student Visa D
summary: Long stay visa for non-EU students. Apply at least 3 months before travel.

other: Detailed requirements and fees were not on the page read. Check the embassy list.

steps: Attend in person with documents and pay the fees

name: Family Reunion Visa D
summary: Family members of a worker or resident apply separately for a family reunion visa D.

other: Conditions were not on the page read. Check the Immigration Office (dofi.ibz.be).

name: Belgian Nationality for Children Born Abroad to a Belgian Parent
summary: A child born abroad is Belgian if a parent was born in Belgium. Otherwise the Belgian parent must make a declaration within 5 years of birth, or before the child turns 5 if neither parent was born in Belgium.

other: Only the Belgian parent can sign the declaration. Other nationality routes (residence, marriage) and dual nationality rules could not be confirmed.
